description.narrative: The project is implemented in Palestine. The main rights holders are Palestinian youth, especially in marginalized areas. Through close cooperation with communities, organizing and capacitating youth and their organisations, campaigns and advocacy, the Palestinian Youth Union aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between Palestinian Youth Union and The Palme Center. Founded in 1992, the Palestinian Youth Union (PYU) is an organisation that works with and in the interest of the Palestinian youth, especially in the marginalised areas, organising and strengthening youth to manage their own situation pertaining to both the occupation and internal Palestinian problems. It has the ability to influence policy and legislation and have a strong standing with grassroots and local organisations, especially on the West Bank.Other Donors to the OrganisationThe previous and the proposed collaboration is a core project. Through this instrument, PYU is able to be more strategic in choosing donor cooperation. Other donors include UNDP, EU and International NGOs. This may vary over years but approved projects for 2020 include EU and two Italian organisations. Submitted projects for 2020 include two EU projects, OCHA, Ministry of Social Development, Welfare Associatoin and the Japaneese Embassy. As a core project, harmonisation is in place and PYU are able to work for synergies themselves. WeEffect have shown interest in collaborating with PYU on specific issues this is welcome and initial discussions with both WeEffect and PYU have been held.Project ObjectiveThe Palestinian Youth Union will empower palestinian youth and help them raise their issues on the political agenda, improve their representation and fight youth unemployment.Actor groupsDecision makers: Local authroties, ministries and legislators. Actors working in cooperation: CBOs including grass roots organisations, cooperatives, women and youth centers, clubs and more. Networks of civil society organisations. Rights Holders: Youth especially from marginalized areas, women and especially young women.
